checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in ME
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Licensed electrical contractor or licensed master electrician pulls the permit — the contractor license information must appear on the application. Because this is commercial fire alarm work, the permit should be filed by the electrical contractor responsible for the system work; the owner does not typically pull this permit.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to City of Portland Permitting & Development (PP&D)

common_mistakes: Submitting the job as a generic electrical repair instead of a commercial fire alarm modification — that can bounce the application or delay review
Not including the sprinkler monitoring details on the submittal — the building department wants to see exactly how supervisory and waterflow signals are handled
Starting panel replacement before the permit is issued and posted — fire alarm work is life-safety work and can be stopped immediately
Failing to coordinate the monitoring company and fire alarm vendor before final inspection — the system can fail acceptance if signals are not verified live

Submitting permit application without verifying current contractor registration status — an expired or lapsed city registration will block your application silently. Verify your registration is current BEFORE submitting.

response_body.inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through Portland PP&D using the city permit portal at or by calling (207) 874-8703. For commercial fire alarm work, book with advance notice and have the permit number, job address, and requested inspection type ready. If the project is tied to fire alarm acceptance testing, coordinate the inspection date with the fire alarm vendor and monitoring company before requesting the final.

pro_tips: Bring the panel cut sheet, battery specs, and monitoring interface details with the permit submittal — commercial fire alarm permits move faster when the reviewer can confirm the exact equipment.
Call the monitoring company before final inspection and have them on standby for live signal verification; that avoids a failed final and a second trip fee.
Check your Portland contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are the #1 avoidable rejection reason.
For a $45,000 commercial life-safety scope, submit a clean riser diagram and device list up front; that usually saves a full review cycle.
